summary: Verification of the UTC->local timezone HH:MM display fix for /asistencia. The fix was NOT actually applied in the UI. The helper `formatHHMM(iso)` was correctly added to /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js, but it is never imported or used in /app/frontend/src/pages/Asistencia.jsx. All 7 display sites (toast, CheckInView row, HubView row count/filter, Resumen view, elapsed-time 'en campo' countdown) still read `r.check_in_hhmm` / `r.check_out_hhmm`, which the backend emits as UTC-based HH:MM strings. Therefore the user's reported bug (phone shows 12:25 local but UI shows 07:25 UTC in UTC+5) will PERSIST. No functional change ships to the browser bundle beyond the unused helper — confirmed by curling the live /static/js/bundle.js: `formatHHMM`=2 occurrences (export only), `check_in_hhmm`=7 occurrences (still consumed). Skipped login/Playwright scan+display assertion because the static/bundle evidence conclusively proves the UI code was not updated.

ui_bugs.issue: Toast still uses res.check_in_hhmm (UTC string) instead of formatHHMM(res.check_in). Line ~113-114.
formatHHMM is not imported from '@/lib/api' (line 8). Must add it to the import.

integration_issues.issue: Elapsed/'en campo' countdown also keyed off the HH:MM UTC string in some branches rather than `r.check_in` ISO; must switch to formatHHMM/new Date(r.check_in) consistently.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Asistencia.jsx add `formatHHMM` to the existing import from '@/lib/api'.
Replace every occurrence of `r.check_in_hhmm` with `formatHHMM(r.check_in)` and `r.check_out_hhmm` with `formatHHMM(r.check_out)` at the display sites (lines ~113, 114, 460, 936, 938, 1086, 1187).

For the boolean guards used to detect open shifts (e.g., `!r.check_out_hhmm` on lines 93, 152, 246, 435, 937, 1086, 1187), keep logical checks on the ISO field: use `!r.check_out` instead of `!r.check_out_hhmm` so logic doesn't depend on legacy field (optional but cleaner).
In the toast: use formatHHMM(res.check_in) and formatHHMM(res.check_out) for the two toast.success calls.

After the swap, retest in a non-UTC TZ by overriding the browser timezone (e.g., Playwright context timezone_id='Asia/Karachi') and asserting the displayed HH:MM equals new Date(iso).toLocaleTimeString([], {hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit',hour12:false}) in that TZ.
critical_code_review_comments: The helper formatHHMM was added but never wired — classic dead-code regression. CI should fail builds where exported helpers in api.js have zero in-repo consumers (eslint no-unused-exports).

Display logic mixes two sources of truth: backend-emitted UTC HH:MM strings (check_in_hhmm) and the ISO `check_in`. Once the migration lands, remove check_in_hhmm/check_out_hhmm from frontend reads entirely to avoid future drift. Backend may keep them for backwards compat as stated.
Boolean 'is open shift' predicates currently rely on `!r.check_out_hhmm`. Prefer `!r.check_out` (ISO) so that if backend ever drops the legacy field the open/closed status still works.
test_credentials: Admin gaelmartin158@gmail.com / agriscan2026 (not exercised this run due to static evidence)
context_for_next_testing_agent: After E1 applies the swap, run Playwright with browser context `timezone_id='Asia/Karachi'` (UTC+5), login as admin, go to /asistencia, select a session, open Check-in tile, use keyboard (K) button to enter a worker id, submit, and assert that (a) the toast HH:MM equals the value returned by page.evaluate(iso => new Date(iso).toLocaleTimeString([], {hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit',hour12:false}), res.check_in) and (b) the row cell in the attendance list shows the same local HH:MM, NOT the raw UTC substring of the ISO. Also verify HubView row and Resumen view show the same local time.
rca of the issue: Root cause: The main agent authored the correct helper `formatHHMM` in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js (converts ISO -> local HH:MM via toLocaleTimeString) but never updated the consumer file /app/frontend/src/pages/Asistencia.jsx. Static grep: `formatHHMM` has 0 occurrences in Asistencia.jsx; `check_in_hhmm` still has 7 and `check_out_hhmm` still has 10. The live production bundle confirms this (formatHHMM=2 export-only references, check_in_hhmm=7 consumer references). Reproduction: Any browser in a non-UTC timezone will still see the UTC HH:MM returned by backend. Mitigation: import `formatHHMM` and swap all 7 display sites + 2 toasts as detailed under action_items; also prefer the ISO field for open/closed shift predicates.
